intro:
A chat turn: an avatar, a bubble, and the metadata around it.

The pieces are separate because conversations differ in which they need. A support thread wants a sender name and a read receipt; an assistant transcript wants neither, but does want the bubble to carry tool output and actions.

For the scroll behaviour around a list of these, use [MessageScroller](/docs/components/message-scroller).
usage:
<Message>
  <Message.Avatar>
    <Avatar size="sm" fallback="KA" />
  </Message.Avatar>
  <Message.Content>
    <Message.Bubble>
      <Message.BubbleContent>How can I help you today?</Message.BubbleContent>
    </Message.Bubble>
  </Message.Content>
</Message>

// The outgoing side.
<Message align="end">
  <Message.Content>
    <Message.Bubble>
      <Message.BubbleContent>Set a reminder for 9am.</Message.BubbleContent>
    </Message.Bubble>
    <Message.Footer>Read</Message.Footer>
  </Message.Content>
</Message>

// Consecutive turns from one sender.
<Message.Group align="start">
  <Message>
    <Message.Avatar><Avatar size="sm" fallback="AI" /></Message.Avatar>
    <Message.Content>
      <Message.Header>Assistant</Message.Header>
      <Message.Bubble>
        <Message.BubbleContent>Looking that up…</Message.BubbleContent>
      </Message.Bubble>
    </Message.Content>
  </Message>
  <Message>
    <Message.Avatar><Avatar size="sm" fallback="AI" /></Message.Avatar>
    <Message.Content>
      <Message.Bubble>
        <Message.BubbleContent>Your reminder is set.</Message.BubbleContent>
      </Message.Bubble>
    </Message.Content>
  </Message>
</Message.Group>

parts.Group: Consecutive turns from one sender. Tightens spacing and stacks them.
parts.Avatar: Slot for the sender avatar. Reserved but emptied on a stacked message.
parts.Content: Column holding the header, bubble, actions and footer.
parts.Header: Sender name or timestamp above the bubble.
parts.Bubble: The speech bubble. Takes its colour and squared corner from align.
parts.BubbleContent: Text inside the bubble, in whichever colour reads against it.
parts.Actions: Row of controls under the bubble — copy, retry, feedback.
parts.Footer: Delivery state or timestamp below the bubble.

notes:
### Alignment

`align` is the only decision the root makes, and every part reads it from context: which side the row sits on, which way the avatar goes, which corner of the bubble is squared off, and which colour it takes. `start` is incoming (muted bubble), `end` is outgoing (primary bubble).

Set it on `Message.Group` instead and every message inside inherits it.

### Grouping

`Message.Group` marks every turn after the first as `stacked`. A stacked message still renders its avatar slot but leaves it empty, so the bubbles stay in one column instead of the second sliding under the first one's avatar. Pass `stacked` on a message explicitly to override that.

### In a list

Render a transcript with an inverted `FlatList`, not a `ScrollView` — it keeps the newest turn pinned to the bottom without measuring content, and recycles rows as the conversation grows.

examples.title: Both sides of a conversation
examples.description: `align` decides the row direction, the avatar side, which bubble corner is squared off, and the bubble colour — every part reads it from context.
examples.code:
<Message>
  <Message.Avatar>
    <Avatar size="sm" source={{ uri: them.avatar }} fallback="OL" />
  </Message.Avatar>
  <Message.Content>
    <Message.Bubble>
      <Message.BubbleContent>How can I help you today?</Message.BubbleContent>
    </Message.Bubble>
  </Message.Content>
</Message>

<Message align="end">
  <Message.Content>
    <Message.Bubble>
      <Message.BubbleContent>Set a reminder for 9am.</Message.BubbleContent>
    </Message.Bubble>
    <Message.Footer>Read</Message.Footer>
  </Message.Content>
</Message>

examples.title: Grouped turns
examples.description: Every turn after the first is marked `stacked`: it keeps its avatar slot but empties it, so the bubbles stay in one column.

examples.title: Actions under the bubble
examples.description: `Message.Actions` reverses its row on the outgoing side so the buttons stay on the message’s own edge.
examples.code:
<Message.Content>
  <Message.Bubble>
    <Message.BubbleContent>{answer}</Message.BubbleContent>
  </Message.Bubble>
  <Message.Actions>
    <Button size="sm" variant="ghost" onPress={() => copy(answer)}>Copy</Button>
    <Button size="sm" variant="ghost" onPress={retry}>Retry</Button>
  </Message.Actions>
</Message.Content>

examples.title: In a transcript
examples.description: An inverted `FlatList` keeps the newest turn pinned to the bottom without measuring content, and recycles rows as the conversation grows.
examples.code:
<FlatList
  data={[...messages].reverse()}
  inverted
  keyExtractor={(m) => m.id}
  contentContainerClassName="gap-3 px-4 py-3"
  renderItem={({ item }) => (
    <Message align={item.role === 'user' ? 'end' : 'start'}>
      <Message.Content>
        <Message.Bubble>
          <Message.BubbleContent>{item.text}</Message.BubbleContent>
        </Message.Bubble>
      </Message.Content>
    </Message>
  )}
/>

examples.title: Long-press for actions
examples.description: Give the turn an `onLongPress` and the whole row becomes a long-press target with the library's press feedback — the gesture a chat uses to surface per-message actions. The component only exposes the gesture; open a sheet or a popover from it.
examples.code:
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<Message align="end" onLongPress={() => setOpen(true)}>
  <Message.Content>
    <Message.Bubble>
      <Message.BubbleContent>Long-press me for actions.</Message.BubbleContent>
    </Message.Bubble>
  </Message.Content>
</Message>

<BottomSheet open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <BottomSheet.Content>
    {/* copy · reply · forward · delete */}
  </BottomSheet.Content>
</BottomSheet>

examples.title: Header and footer
examples.description: `Message.Header` names the speaker above the bubble; `Message.Footer` timestamps it below.
examples.code:
<Message>
  <Message.Avatar>
    <Avatar size="sm" source={{ uri: user.avatar }} fallback="OL" />
  </Message.Avatar>
  <Message.Content>
    <Message.Header>Olivia</Message.Header>
    <Message.Bubble>
      <Message.BubbleContent>I pushed the fix — can you take another look?</Message.BubbleContent>
    </Message.Bubble>
    <Message.Footer>Yesterday at 18:04</Message.Footer>
  </Message.Content>
</Message>
